name: Mikey Reaves
notes: The current-generation Nashville track-builder, working sample-and-loop-first inside a live-music town. His method is quoted and is "deliberately anti-perfectionist and directly implementable": "there's a very basic track. Write a song to it, and the rest will reveal itself," and "I try not to make it over-complicated; I try to just keep it fast-moving and make quick decisions. So: start from a skeletal programmed groove (clap backbeat, simple hat, one kick pattern), let the song dictate the rest, and swap in the live kit at the chorus." That is a single kick pattern, one hat subdivision, a low perc count and a real `fullTimeVariantProb` for the chorus swap — a deliberately thin skeleton rather than a dense one. The 808 is authored in `counter_riff` because the entry gives each layer a section: "sub-first low end in the skeleton, with electric bass added later; the sub carries the verse, the band carries the chorus." Harmony is "loop-based and static — two-bar I–V–vi–IV or vi–IV–I–V under sustained pads," concentrated "around C/G/E♭." The loop-design constraint is the melodic parameter and it is unusually precise: loops are chosen for having "enough interesting melodic content to spark something, but not so much that nothing you sing will work," i.e. "sparse, harmonically-open, stackable two-bar cells" — hence the low density, the high `emptyBarBias`, the high two-bar cell repeat and a `chordToneBias` deliberately below the genre's so the cell leaves room for a vocal. ⚠ Confidence is medium (research: medium-high). ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are the 808 register, the full-time variant share and the counter ratio. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 940/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.3 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "he builds from sample packs treated as "songstarters and production Lego pieces" — loops chosen for having "enough interesting melodic content to spark something, but not so much that nothing you sing will work," which is a genuinely useful constraint on loop design: sparse, harmonically-open, stackable two-bar cells.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
